surprise.title: 137 years ago this morning, Nellie Bly set out to beat Around the World in Eighty Days
surprise.body: At 9:40 AM on November 14, 1889, the New York World reporter Nellie Bly boarded the steamer Augusta Victoria with only two days' notice and started a 24,898-mile trip around the globe, trying to turn Jules Verne's novel into fact. A year earlier her editor had doubted she could do it, arguing she only spoke English, would pack too much, and would need a male escort. She went anyway, traveling almost entirely alone through England, France (where she stopped in Amiens to meet Jules Verne himself), the Suez Canal, Ceylon, Singapore, Hong Kong, and Japan. She was back in New York on January 25, 1890, just over 72 days later, a world record. Your own next voyage is far shorter and much comfier: 29 days until you sail out of Tampa on December 13. Today is clear and crisp in Tallahassee, about 40°F early, a high near 59°F, with sunset at 5:40 PM.
